ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the vertices $C$ and $A$ of the square $ABCO$ are on the $x$-axis and $y$-axis, respectively. $BC$ is the diagonal of the rhombus $BDCE$. If $\angle D = 60^\circ$ and $BC = 2$, what are the coordinates of point $D$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As illustrated, draw line DF perpendicular to BC at point F from point D,\\
$\because$ rhombus BDCE,\\
$\therefore$ BD = CD,\\
Also $\because$ $\angle$D = 60$^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$BDC is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DFC = 90$^\circ$, BF = CF = 1, so the y-coordinate of point D is: 1,\\
$\therefore$ in $\triangle$DFC, DF = $\sqrt{CD^{2}-CF^{2}} = \sqrt{2^{2}-1^{2}} = \sqrt{3}$,\\
$\because$ square ABCD, BC = 2,\\
$\therefore$ OC = 2,\\
$\therefore$ the x-coordinate of point D is: OC + DF = 2 + $\sqrt{3}$,\\
Thus, the answer is: $(2+\sqrt{3}, 1) = \boxed{(2+\sqrt{3}, 1)}$.

推理：因为 ABCO 是正方形且 BC=2，所以 OC=2，可取 C=(2,0)，B=(2,2)。设菱形两条对角线 BC 与 DE 的交点为 M。菱形的对角线互相垂直且互相平分，所以 M 是 BC 的中点，M=(2,1)，且 D 在过 M 的水平线上。又因为菱形的对角线 DE 平分顶角 D，而 ∠D=60°，所以 ∠BDM=30°。在直角三角形 DBM 中，BM=1，tan 30°=BM/DM=1/DM，因此 DM=√3。图中 D 在 BC 右侧，所以 D 的横坐标为 2+√3，纵坐标为 1。因此 D=(2+√3,1)。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, the vertices $C$ and $A$ of the square $ABCO$ are on the $x$-axis and $y$-axis, respectively. $BC$ is the diagonal of the rhombus $BDCE$. If $\angle D = 60^\circ$ and $BC = 2$, what are the coordinates of point $D$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As illustrated, draw line $DF$ perpendicular to $BC$ at point $F$ from point $D$.\\
$\because$ rhombus $BDCE$,\\
$\therefore$ $BD = CD$.\\
Also $\because$ $\angle D = 60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle BDC$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle DFC = 90^\circ$, $BF = CF = 1$, so the y-coordinate of point $D$ is $1$.\\
$\therefore$ in $\triangle DFC$, $DF = \sqrt{CD^{2}-CF^{2}} = \sqrt{2^{2}-1^{2}} = \sqrt{3}$.\\
$\because$ square $ABCD$, $BC = 2$,\\
$\therefore$ $OC = 2$.\\
$\therefore$ the x-coordinate of point $D$ is $OC + DF = 2 + \sqrt{3}$.\\
Thus, the answer is $\boxed{(2+\sqrt{3}, 1)}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, O is at the origin, OC is along the positive direction of the x-axis, OA is along the positive direction of the y-axis; ABCO is a square, C is on the x-axis, A is on the y-axis, and BC is the vertical side on the right side of the square. In the figure, with the vertical line segment BC as one diagonal, a rhombus BDCE is drawn, point D is located on the right side of BC, and point E is located on the left side of BC. Reasoning: It is known that BC = 2, so the side length of the square is 2, therefore C = (2, 0), B = (2, 2). In rhombus BDCE, adjacent sides BD = CD. Also because angle D, namely ∠BDC, is 60°, triangle BDC is an isosceles triangle with vertex angle 60°, and thus all three angles are 60°, that is, triangle BDC is an equilateral triangle, with all side lengths equal to 2. Equilateral triangle BDC takes the vertical line segment BC as one side, and point D is on the right side of BC; the midpoint height of BC is y = 1. The horizontal distance from point D to line BC is the height of the equilateral triangle, namely sqrt(2^2 - 1^2) = sqrt(3). Since the line where BC lies is x = 2, and D is on the right side, the x-coordinate of D is 2 + sqrt(3), and the y-coordinate is 1.
